readme: Reviewed exceptions to the JavaScript dependency advisory gate. See .claude/rules/dependency-security.md before editing. Checked by scripts/audit-gate.mjs.

exceptions.rationale: node-forge is reached only through @expo/cli: `expo run:ios` code-signing helpers (`run/ios/codeSigning/Security.js`) and the dev-server manifest signing in `utils/codesigning.js`, which signs the manifests the dev client fetches during `expo start`. The advisory is in RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 signature *verification*; the CLI only signs and generates certificates, and verification of EAS Update manifests happens natively in expo-updates, not in this package. @expo/cli is a developer-machine tool pulled in transitively by `expo` and is in no release bundle. The advisory names `>=1.4.1` as patched and npm has no such version — `latest` is 1.4.0 — so the existing `node-forge@1` override cannot close it; drop this entry once 1.4.1 is published and the override picks it up.

extract-zip is the unpacker @electron/packager runs once per `electron-forge package`/`make` to unzip the Electron binary it downloaded from GitHub releases into the bundle; it executes on a developer machine or the CI packaging job only and ships in no app. The archive it opens is the official Electron release zip for the pinned version, not user input. The advisory names `>=2.0.2` as patched and npm has no such version — `latest` is 2.0.1 — so no `overrides` entry can close this.

Same package and same reachability as GHSA-7pqw-9j4j-h8q3: @electron/packager's one-shot unpacker for the official Electron release zip at packaging time, never in a shipped app. No patched version exists on npm (`latest` is 2.0.1), so an override cannot close it.

undici is reached only at build time on a developer machine or the CI packaging job: @electron/get runs it to download the pinned Electron binary from GitHub releases, and node-gyp runs it while compiling the native keychain addon. Neither path is in a shipped app bundle — the desktop renderer installs its own XHR-based IsomorphicEventSource and never bundles undici. The advisory is a DoS via an unhandled error on excessive content-encodings from the servers the tool talks to (GitHub releases / the Node headers mirror), not attacker-controlled input. electron and node-gyp are devDependencies, so both paths are dev-graph. Patched is >=7.30.1 / >=6.29.1, reachable only through electron's and node-gyp's own transitive ranges; drop this entry once they resolve the patched undici.

happy-dom is the DOM environment for vitest, used only by `pnpm test` (devDependency in @safely/ux and @safely/web-ui, transitive via vitest elsewhere). It runs on a developer machine and in the test CI job, never in a shipped bundle. The advisory is host code execution via an unsanitized import alias; the only code happy-dom evaluates here is this repository's own test suite, not untrusted input. Patched is >=21.0.4, a major bump from the 20.x line deferred to avoid a test-runtime major mid-release — upgrade happy-dom to >=21.0.4 and drop this entry.

Our own runtime zod is pinned to 4.6.6 through the workspace `catalog:`, so no shipped bundle carries the vulnerable version. The copies the advisory still matches are transitive tooling only: zod 3.25.76 throughout @expo/cli (Expo's dev/build CLI, in the production graph because `expo` is a transitive dependency of apps/mobile but never bundled into a release), and zod 4.4.1 under eslint-plugin-react-hooks / zod-validation-error (lint, dev only). The advisory is a memory-exhaustion DoS while validating oversized constrained collections; the only schemas these tools parse are their own CLI arguments and lint config at dev/build time, not attacker-controlled data in the wallet. Drop this entry once @expo/cli and the eslint plugins resolve zod >=4.6.6.
